name: Brix Digital Signage
description: Hosted MCP server for Brix digital signage: check screen health and why a screen is blank, put playlists and announcements on screens, take over screens for emergencies, upload media, build playlists and schedules, and pull uptime and proof-of-play reports. Sign in with OAuth or use an API key.
author: Brix Signage

tools.name: list_items
tools.description:
List items of one kind with their ids, so other tools can act on them.

When to use:
- A request names a screen, file, playlist or location and you need its id.
- Seeing what runs now (casts, emergencies), what is wrong now (alerts), approval requests, deleted items (recycle_bin), or who is in the workspace and what they may do (people, roles).

When NOT to use:
- Reading one item's contents: use get_items.
- History over time: use get_fleet_report.

What to know:
- Rows are short (id, name, nodeId, counts), never configs or members; only locations this connection can see. people rows add each person's role at each location (never sign-in details); roles rows add their permissions.
- A kind this connection cannot read is an error, not an empty list. people and roles are read-only here (invite with create_items); changing a person's access, roles, API keys and billing stays with a signed-in person in the Brix console, so a connected app can never widen access. To see what this connection itself may do, use get_items kind account.
- media, alerts and recycle_bin come newest first. Every call counts toward the connection's 30 tool calls a minute, so page with offset instead of re-listing.

Parameters:
- kind: the list to read; app_types and connectors are what create_items can make. A connectors row's setup is here (create_items makes it) or console (a person connects it in the Brix console, and it is then used by its id).
- Filters (all optional, combined with AND, ignored on kinds they do not name): q (name contains, any kind but people and roles); status (screens online/offline/pairing; approvals pending by default, approved, rejected, withdrawn); nodeId (screens at that location and below; alerts at that location only); tag (screens, media); mediaKind and folderId (media); severity and screenId (alerts); binKind (recycle_bin).
- limit: page size for media and approvals (default 50); other kinds give 100 a page. offset: pass nextOffset while hasMore.
- Example: {kind:"screens", status:"offline", nodeId:"on_west"}.

tools.name: get_items
tools.description:
Read items of one kind in full.

When to use:
- Before update_items, to see current values and part ids (playlist items pli_…, schedule blocks sb_…).
- Checking how many rows of a sheet a repeating creative plays, and how many fit.
- Checking an approval request, a fired emergency, a device test run, a person's locations and roles, a role's permissions, or who this connection is (kind account).

When NOT to use:
- Searching by name: use list_items first.
- Why a screen is blank, its outages or its TV state: use get_screen_status (get_items returns a screen's settings and assigned content).

What to know:
- Returns a playlist's items in order, a schedule's blocks, a layout's zones, an app's config, a screen's status and content.
- A creative that repeats for each row also returns repeatStatus: rowCount and rowsThatFit (what the last sync holds and how many play), limitedBy (rows, bytes or null), loopSeconds, columns (each header and its row tag), missingColumns, firstRowBindings, lastSyncedAt and warnings to pass on. rowCount is null when this connection cannot read that data source.
- Sign-in details of feeds and web links stay in the Brix console: a stored one reads as ••••••••, never as its value. Items outside this connection's locations read as not found.

Parameters:
- kind: the kind of every id. account takes no ids and returns this connection's actor, workspace and permissions.
- ids: prefix-typed ids from list_items (pl_… playlist, scr_… screen, sch_… schedule); required for every kind but account. Each id returns its item or not found; the rest still return.
- device_test_runs: call again until status is finished.
- Example: {kind:"playlists", ids:["pl_8f2c"]}.

tools.name: create_items
tools.description:
Create new items of one kind.

When to use:
- Adding anything new, uploading files (media_files for bytes you hold, media_from_urls for public links), pairing a device by its code or inviting a person.

When NOT to use:
- Changing an existing item: use update_items.
- Showing it on screens: create it, then use set_screen_content or start_takeover.

What to know:
- playlists, schedules, locations and creatives are all-or-nothing: one bad row rejects the call and names it (a location whose externalId exists is skipped, so imports re-run safely). Other kinds are created one by one; each reports ok or its error and the rest continue.
- New content at a location under review starts as a draft. Needs the kind's create permission there.
- Tools never take sign-in values: a data_sources or apps item holding one, or a feed that cannot work without one, is refused and nothing is created. A person connects those in the Brix console; the feed is then used by its id.
- Repeat for each row: one design and one data source play as a slideshow, one slide per row of the sheet. Set dataSourceId and repeat {over:"rows", secondsPerRow:12}; seconds run from 3 to 3600, default 12. A workspace without this feature refuses it with 403 feature_disabled and saves nothing, so tell the person instead of retrying.
- Row tags follow the slide: {{row.column}} in a text box's text, row.column in a field box's field, {{row.photo}} as an image box's url or the backgroundUrl. {{rows.0.column}} stays on the sheet's first row on every slide.
- The column name in a row tag is the sheet's header in lower case with accents removed, every other character changed to _, repeats collapsed and none at the ends: Date de début is row.date_de_debut, Région (€) is row.region. A missing column or an empty cell reads blank.
- A picture cell must be a plain https address; anything else leaves that box empty on that slide.
- At most 200 rows and 3 MB of slides play, and each slide is a whole copy of the design, so a large design fits fewer rows. Afterwards read it with get_items: repeatStatus gives rowCount, rowsThatFit, limitedBy, columns, missingColumns and warnings. Tell the person when rowsThatFit is below rowCount.
- It reaches screens like any design: set_screen_content or start_takeover with contentKind creative, a schedule block or a layout zone. A playlist item has its own switch: appendItems with refKind creative may answer 403 feature_disabled, and then set_screen_content still works.

Parameters:
- Pass exactly one array; its name is the kind and two arrays is an error.
- Ids inside items (refId, contentId, nodeId, screenId, appKey, connector) must already exist; get them from list_items.
- Example: {playlists:[{name:"Lobby loop", items:[{refKind:"media", refId:"med_logo", durationSec:10}]}]}.

nodeId.description: Location id; omit for the workspace root.

tools.name: update_items
tools.description:
Change existing items of one kind, the same changes on every id.

When to use:
- Renaming, moving or retagging items; editing what is inside a playlist, schedule, layout or screen group; screen, web link and data feed settings; swapping a screen's device; closing an alert.
- Turning Repeat for each row on, changing its seconds or turning it off on a creative (repeat, useEachRow).
- Franchise menus: share a creative live with child workspaces (shareWithWorkspaces), and set one location's own prices on a creative shared to it (localText) while the owner's design keeps updating.

When NOT to use:
- Showing content on screens: use set_screen_content.
- New items: use create_items. Removing: use delete_items.

What to know:
- Per id, changes run as steps in a fixed order and stop at that id's first failure; earlier steps stay and are named; other ids go on. Each id returns the item as it is now.
- Content that airs where review is required goes back to draft. Needs the kind's edit permission (screen moves: at both locations).
- Changes go live at once: every screen playing an edited playlist, schedule or layout shows the new version at its next sync. There is no undo; overwritten values and removed playlist items are gone, so note the old values with get_items first.
- Repeat for each row: one design and one data source play as a slideshow, one slide per row of the sheet. Set dataSourceId and repeat {over:"rows", secondsPerRow:12}; seconds run from 3 to 3600, default 12. A workspace without this feature refuses it with 403 feature_disabled and saves nothing, so tell the person instead of retrying.
- Row tags follow the slide: {{row.column}} in a text box's text, row.column in a field box's field, {{row.photo}} as an image box's url or the backgroundUrl. {{rows.0.column}} stays on the sheet's first row on every slide.
- The column name in a row tag is the sheet's header in lower case with accents removed, every other character changed to _, repeats collapsed and none at the ends: Date de début is row.date_de_debut, Région (€) is row.region. A missing column or an empty cell reads blank.
- A picture cell must be a plain https address; anything else leaves that box empty on that slide.
- At most 200 rows and 3 MB of slides play, and each slide is a whole copy of the design, so a large design fits fewer rows. Afterwards read it with get_items: repeatStatus gives rowCount, rowsThatFit, limitedBy, columns, missingColumns and warnings. Tell the person when rowsThatFit is below rowCount.
- It reaches screens like any design: set_screen_content or start_takeover with contentKind creative, a schedule block or a layout zone. A playlist item has its own switch: appendItems with refKind creative may answer 403 feature_disabled, and then set_screen_content still works.
- repeat:null turns it off and the design plays once; its row tags then have no row to read, so change them to {{rows.0.column}} in the same call's boxes.

Parameters:
- kind and ids: every id must be of that kind; get them from list_items. Every id gets identical changes; for different values per item, call once per value.
- changes: only the fields to change. Each field's description names the kinds that take it; a field the kind does not take is refused before anything changes.
- zones, boxes, config and tags replace the whole value: read it with get_items first. In config, a value that reads •••••••• (sent back or left out) keeps what is stored; a new sign-in value, or clearing one, is refused because a person changes those in the Brix console.
- Example: {kind:"screens", ids:["scr_lobby7", "scr_lobby8"], changes:{nodeId:"on_store12", tags:["lobby"]}}.

nodeId.description: Move to this location (list_items kind locations); null = workspace root. screens (refused when what it plays needs approval there), playlists, schedules, layouts, creatives, apps, data_sources, media, media_folders.

Refused (feature_disabled) where the workspace does not have playlist transitions yet. playlists.

autoFullscreenForVideo.description: A video in any zone fills the whole screen while it plays. layouts.

boxes.description: All layers of the creative, same box shape as create_items creatives. creatives.

Only boxes the owner left editable (get_items shows each box's shareLock); other edits are refused. Boxes not named keep their local text. creatives.

contentKind.description: emergency_templates: kind of content to show.

tools.name: delete_items
tools.description:
Delete items of one kind into the 30-day recycle bin.

When to use:
- The person has confirmed what should go (show it with list_items or get_items first).

When NOT to use:
- Taking a screen out of a group: use update_items removeScreenIds.
- Stopping a takeover: use end_takeover.

What to know:
- restore_items undoes a delete within 30 days. A deleted playlist or schedule stops on every screen playing it; a deleted screen's device returns to pairing; a deleted location hands its content to its parent.
- Refused: the root, a location with child locations, items shared to another workspace. Each id reports ok or its error. Needs the kind's delete permission.

Parameters:
- kind and ids: every id must be of that kind.
- permanent: true erases for good instead (recycle-bin kinds only). The first call deletes nothing and returns wouldErase and a confirmCode.
- confirmCode: only with permanent:true; send the code from the first call, after the person says yes, with the same kind and ids. It lasts 10 minutes and fits only those ids; without permanent it is an error.
- Example: {kind:"playlists", ids:["pl_8f2c"]}.

tools.name: restore_items
tools.description:
Bring back deleted items of one kind from the 30-day recycle bin.

When to use:
- Undoing delete_items.

When NOT to use:
- Items deleted more than 30 days ago: they are gone and report not found.

What to know:
- Whatever used a restored item (playlists, screens) uses it again; a restored screen re-pairs by itself if its device still holds its pairing. Each id reports ok or not found. Needs the kind's delete permission.

Parameters:
- kind: the list_items kind name, so a recycle_bin row of kind playlist is restored with kind playlists.
- ids: up to 50, from list_items kind recycle_bin. An id that is not in the bin reports "not in the recycle bin"; one deleted over 30 days ago reports not found.
- Example: {kind:"playlists", ids:["pl_8f2c"]}.

tools.name: set_screen_content
tools.description:
Set what screens play by default until it is changed again.

When to use:
- Putting a playlist, schedule, app, media file or creative on one screen, a list, or every screen under a location.

When NOT to use:
- A takeover that ends by itself: use start_takeover.
- Changing what a playlist contains: use update_items (every screen playing it follows).

What to know:
- Screens update within seconds. In a bulk call, screens the content is not shared to or whose location needs approval for it are skipped and counted (notShared, needsApproval); the rest change. Needs screen.cast.

Parameters:
- screenId, screenIds and nodeId (every screen at and under it, up to 1000): give at least one; they combine into one set.
- contentKind: playlist, schedule, app, media or creative. null clears what plays and needs exactly one screen and no nodeId.
- contentId: the playlist, schedule, app, media or creative id from list_items; omit only with contentKind null.
- Example: {nodeId:"on_ca", contentKind:"playlist", contentId:"pl_spring"}.

tools.name: start_takeover
tools.description:
Show something on screens over their normal content, now.

When to use:
- Existing content for a while (the lunch menu until 2 pm), or a pre-armed emergency.

When NOT to use:
- A lasting change: use set_screen_content.

What to know:
- Content ends by itself; an emergency stays above everything until end_takeover, so confirm its scope with the person first. Returns castId for end_takeover. Needs screen.cast.

Parameters:
- Pass exactly one of: contentId with contentKind (from list_items), or emergencyTemplateId (from list_items kind emergency_templates).
- scopeKind: all (default, every screen this connection reaches), node with scopeNodeId, or screens with screenIds. An emergency ignores scope and uses its template's.
- expiresAt: ISO 8601 with offset, default one hour from now.
- Example: {contentKind:"playlist", contentId:"pl_lunch", scopeKind:"node", scopeNodeId:"on_store12", expiresAt:"2026-10-20T14:00:00-07:00"}.

tools.name: end_takeover
tools.description:
End a running takeover or emergency on every screen it covers, in one call.

When to use:
- Taking down what start_takeover started, early.

When NOT to use:
- Changing default content: use set_screen_content.
- Calling once per screen: one call ends it everywhere.

What to know:
- Screens return to their normal content at once. Ending one that already ended succeeds with alreadyEnded:true; an unknown id fails and lists what is running. Needs screen.cast (emergency-override.create for an emergency).

Parameters:
- castId: the castId start_takeover returned, an emergency id (emg_…), the id of the content on screen, or the takeover's exact headline. The last two end every running takeover of it. Find running ones with list_items kind casts or emergencies.

tools.name: get_screen_status
tools.description:
Explain the state of one screen.

When to use:
- Why a screen shows what it shows, why it is blank or wrong, when it was down, or what its TV did.

When NOT to use:
- A screen's settings, tags or assigned content: use get_items kind screens.
- Many screens: use get_fleet_report. A picture: use capture_screenshot. A fix: use control_screens.

What to know:
- Reads what the screen already reported and never contacts it, so it answers for offline screens. Needs screen.view.

Parameters:
- screenId: one scr_… id from list_items kind screens.
- view: why (the source on screen: deactivated, emergency, takeover, schedule or default); diagnose (likely cause plus a checklist; guided:true marks a TV/input/cable guess, not a reading); outages (each outage with length and cause); tv (TV off, other input, cable lost; Signage Sticks only).
- days: outages default 30; tv default and max 14. limit: default 50; max 200 for outages, 500 for tv. Both are ignored for why and diagnose.
- Example: {screenId:"scr_lobby7", view:"outages", days:7}.

tools.name: capture_screenshot
tools.description:
Take a new screenshot of one screen and return it as an image; nothing on the screen changes.

When to use:
- Checking what a screen shows, e.g. after set_screen_content or control_screens.

When NOT to use:
- Learning why: use get_screen_status. Polling in a loop.

What to know:
- Waits up to about 5 seconds; a slow or offline screen returns its last frame with fresh:false. A frame over 2 MB returns latestFrameUrl only. Needs screen.edit (it sends a device command).

Parameters:
- screenId: one scr_… id from list_items kind screens; for several screens, call once each. An id outside this connection's reach reads as not found and nothing is sent.

tools.name: control_screens
tools.description:
Send a device action to one or many screens.

When to use:
- A change has not appeared, a screen is frozen, an old or broken file keeps playing, or the TV must go on or off.

When NOT to use:
- Changing content: use set_screen_content. New data from a feed or web page: use refresh_data.

What to know:
- Devices act within seconds; offline ones act when they come back. Check the result with capture_screenshot. Needs screen.edit.

Parameters:
- action: refresh (reload content, no restart; try first), reboot (restart; about a minute blank), clear_cache (delete stored files so they download again; media shows late meanwhile), tv_on or tv_off (HDMI-CEC TVs only; the player keeps running).
- screenId and screenIds: give either or both; they combine into one set, each screen gets the action once, and screens out of reach are skipped.
- Example: {action:"refresh", screenIds:["scr_7", "scr_8"]}.

tools.name: review_approval
tools.description:
Approve, reject or withdraw one pending approval request.

When to use:
- This connection's person is an approver and a request is waiting (list_items kind approvals; read it with get_items kind approvals).
- Cancelling a request that is no longer wanted, or one left behind by a person who has gone: withdraw.

When NOT to use:
- Editing the content: use update_items (an edit opens a new request).

What to know:
- approve airs the content where it is assigned, at once; reject keeps it off screens; withdraw closes the request with no decision and puts the content back to draft. Each is final.
- approve and reject need this connection's person to be an approver in the request's chain; withdraw needs the requester or such an approver. Otherwise the call is refused.

Parameters:
- approvalId: an ar_… id from list_items kind approvals.
- reason: required with reject and shown to the requester word for word; with approve, an optional note; ignored with withdraw.
- Example: {approvalId:"ar_12", decision:"reject", reason:"Price on slide 2 is wrong."}.

tools.name: refresh_data
tools.description:
Pull fresh content now instead of at the next scheduled refresh.

When to use:
- Before an announcement, so menus and prices are current; after someone edits a sheet that a creative repeats over; after changing a web link's crop with update_items, to see the result.

When NOT to use:
- Changing a feed's or link's settings: use update_items. A screen that has not picked up a change, or is frozen: use control_screens.

What to know:
- Settings never change. A failing feed is reported in the result, not thrown. Screens showing the data update when a sync succeeds. Needs integration.edit for feeds, media.edit for a web link.
- A sheet published to the web changes on Google's side up to about 5 minutes after an edit, so a sync straight after an edit can still read the old rows: synced true says the sync ran, not that the edit arrived. Check rowCount with get_items and sync again after a few minutes if it is old.

Parameters:
- Pass exactly one; none or two is an error.
- dataSourceId: one ds_… feed from list_items kind data_sources.
- allDataSources: true syncs every feed you can edit, one after another; one failure does not stop the rest; limited to 5 calls a minute.
- webLinkId: one med_… web link (list_items kind media, mediaKind web); renders a new snapshot.

tools.name: get_fleet_report
tools.description:
Read a report across screens for a time window.

When to use:
- Uptime and outage causes, what actually played, or who changed what.

When NOT to use:
- One screen's detail: use get_screen_status. What is wrong now: use list_items kind alerts.

What to know:
- Reads stored history only; only screens this connection can see count. Needs screen.view (uptime), playback-log.view (proof_of_play) or audit-log.view (audit_log).

Parameters:
- report: uptime (online % per screen, outages with causes, worst first, one-line insights), proof_of_play (plays, watch time, skips and failures per content, and where) or audit_log (who changed what, newest first, by name).
- from and to: uptime and proof_of_play only; ISO 8601; default the whole stored window (30 days for uptime) up to now; a non-ISO value is refused. screenId: uptime and proof_of_play only, one screen. screenIds, contentIds and detail: proof_of_play only.
- since, limit (default 50) and cursor (nextCursor of the previous page): audit_log only.
- Parameters for another report are ignored. Example: {report:"uptime", from:"2026-10-13T00:00:00Z"}.

screenIds.description: proof_of_play: only these screens, for example every screen at one venue.

contentIds.description: proof_of_play: only these content ids, for example one advertiser's ads.

detail.description: proof_of_play: screens adds byScreen, one row per content and screen.

tools.name: mint_upload_url
tools.description: Get a one-shot upload URL for a large file. The model's host PUTs bytes to it then calls confirm_media_upload with the same `uploadId`.

contentType.description: MIME type of the file, e.g. video/mp4 or image/png.

tools.name: confirm_media_upload
tools.description: Finalize an upload after PUTting bytes to a mint_upload_url. Creates the media_assets row.

uploadId.description: The upl_… id that mint_upload_url returned.

folderId.description: Library folder to file it in; omit for the library root.

tags.description: Tags to set on the new asset.
